<header class="c-pagehead">
  <div class="c-wrap">
<h1>Governance &amp; accountability</h1>
    <p>
      A volunteer centre asks people to work without pay. The least it owes them
      in return is to write down what it expects, what they get, and what happens
      when either side falls short. Those documents are public, and so is every
      change made to them.
    </p>
  </div>
</header>

<section class="c-slab c-slab--paper">
  <div class="c-wrap">
    <div class="c-split">
      <div class="c-prose">

        <h2>Where the centre sits</h2>
        <p>
          CHIRAL is the research arm of the DeepBio ecosystem, alongside
          <strong>DeepBio Limited</strong>, which provides bioinformatics and data
          services as a company, and <strong>DeepBio Academy</strong>, which runs
          training. The three are governed separately because membership means
          different things in each: employment, volunteering, and enrolment
          respectively.
        </p>
        <p>
          That separation matters for reading anything on this page. CHIRAL's
          rules — unpaid positions, minimum commitment, authorship conditions —
          are research-specific. They do not govern DeepBio Limited employees or
          Academy trainees, and are not applied to them.
        </p>

        <h2>Positions are unpaid, and that shapes everything</h2>
        <p>
          Every position at CHIRAL, Research Assistant and Group Leader alike, is
          voluntary and unpaid. It is a research and training opportunity, not
          employment. Nobody is offered a salary, a stipend, or any financial
          benefit.
        </p>
        <p>
          In return the centre provides mentorship, training, access to
          infrastructure, co-authorship on work a member genuinely contributed to,
          and — on satisfactory completion — a recommendation letter. Because the
          position is unpaid, those four things are also the only levers the
          centre has if commitments are not met. They are earned, and they can be
          withheld.
        </p>

        <h2>Who answers to whom</h2>
        <p>
          The Director leads the centre. Each unit is led by a Group Leader who
          reports to the Director, and Research Assistants work within a unit under
          their Group Leader. Every member knows who they report to and what their
          role is expected to produce.
        </p>
        <p>
          Centre-wide policy takes precedence over any unit's own overlay. A unit
          may add rules for its own tools, data types and stack; where the two
          conflict, the centre document wins unless the Director approves a
          documented exception.
        </p>

        <h2>How someone joins</h2>
        <p>
          Entry runs through a prerequisite course, then an interview — not
          through who you know. A candidate completes the DeepBio Academy course
          required for the unit they are applying to, applies with proof of
          completion and a written disclosure of outside commitments, interviews
          with the unit's Group Leader, and is selected by the Group Leader with
          the Director's approval. The first three months are probationary.
        </p>
        <p>
          Completing the course makes someone eligible, not selected — selection is
          competitive. The required course, the proof, the interview outcome and
          the decision are recorded for every recruit, so selection can be
          examined after the fact.
        </p>

        <h2>Authorship is earned against a published standard</h2>
        <p>
          Authorship follows the four
          <a href="https://www.icmje.org/recommendations/browse/roles-and-responsibilities/defining-the-role-of-authors-and-contributors.html">ICMJE criteria</a>,
          all of which must be met. Gift, guest and ghost authorship are
          prohibited. Roles are discussed at the start of a project and revisited
          as contributions change, each author's specific contribution is recorded
          using CRediT, and seniority does not buy a place on a paper.
        </p>
        <p>
          This is the mechanism behind the claim made elsewhere on this site that
          students first-author their own work. It is written down so it can be
          held against us.
        </p>

        <h2>When things go wrong</h2>
        <p>
          Missed revisions, unexcused absences and missed communication windows
          follow a graded ladder rather than arbitrary judgement. A first lapse is
          a logged reminder; a second is a written warning with a catch-up plan; a
          third triggers an authorship review against the ICMJE criteria; persistent
          or severe lapses mean removal from the project and referral to the
          Director. Penalties affect only the member who lapsed — they never reduce
          the credit of people who did the work.
        </p>
        <p>
          Research misconduct, disputes over authorship, and appeals each have their
          own written procedure in the Publication &amp; Authorship Policy.
        </p>

        <h2>Health data</h2>
        <p>
          No identifiable human data is collected or analysed without ethics
          approval, and data is used only for the purpose the participant consented
          to. Sensitive data lives in encrypted, access-controlled storage — never
          personal laptops, personal cloud drives or personal inboxes — with access
          granted by name on a least-privilege basis and revoked at offboarding.
          Identifiers are separated from analysis datasets, precise household
          coordinates are treated as identifying, and no identifiable data or
          credentials go into Git.
        </p>

        <h2>How these documents change</h2>
        <p>
          They are living documents, kept in the same public repository as this
          website. Anyone can propose a change by opening a pull request, and every
          revision carries an author, a date and a rationale in the history. What
          the centre required of a member in a given month can be reconstructed
          exactly.
        </p>

      </div>

      <div class="c-aside">
        <dl class="c-facts">
          <dt>Positions</dt>
          <dd>Voluntary and unpaid. No salary or stipend, at any level.</dd>

          <dt>Minimum commitment</dt>
          <dd>18 months active; 2 years expected. Authorship is contingent on honouring it.</dd>

          <dt>Probation</dt>
          <dd>First 3 months.</dd>

          <dt>Authorship standard</dt>
          <dd>ICMJE, all four criteria. CRediT roles recorded per author.</dd>

          <dt>Entry route</dt>
          <dd>Prerequisite DeepBio Academy course, then interview and selection.</dd>

          <dt>Ethics</dt>
          <dd>Required before any identifiable human data is touched.</dd>

          <dt>Raising a concern</dt>
          <dd><a href="mailto:chiralbd@gmail.com?subject=Governance%20enquiry">chiralbd@gmail.com</a></dd>
        </dl>

        <p style="margin-top:1.5rem">
          <a class="c-btn c-btn--dark" href="https://github.com/chiralbd/chiralbd.github.io/tree/main/onboarding">Read the full handbook</a>
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="c-slab c-slab--panel">

    <div class="c-slab-head">
      <span class="c-eyebrow">Commitments</span>
      <h2 class="c-h2">What we hold ourselves to</h2>
    </div>
    <ul class="c-rule-list">
      <li><strong>Students first-author their own work.</strong> Authorship is judged against the ICMJE criteria, not against seniority.</li>
      <li><strong>Nobody pays, and nobody is paid.</strong> There are no fees to join and no stipends, at any level of the centre.</li>
      <li><strong>Selection is recorded.</strong> The prerequisite, the interview outcome and the decision are kept for every recruit.</li>
      <li><strong>Consequences are graded and written down</strong> — the same ladder for everyone, applied only to the person who lapsed.</li>
      <li><strong>Health data is not touched without ethics approval</strong>, and is used only for the purpose consented to.</li>
      <li><strong>The rules are public and versioned.</strong> Every change to them is a public commit.</li>
    </ul>
